_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); cruise-line signals

pit_profile.why: Royal Caribbean: 'We are the world’s second largest cruise company operating 39 ships in the cruise vacation industry across five brands with an aggregate capacity of approximately 92,650 berths as of December 31, 2011'; 'We compete principally on the basis of exceptional service provided by our crew, innovation and quality of ships, variety of itineraries, choice of destinations and price'; 'We may lose business to competitors throughout the vacation market'; and 'The demand for cruises is affected by international, national and local economic and geopolitical conditions' (its own FY2011 10-K): a cruise-fleet franchise whose demand follows the economies it sells into, by its own account; no disruption theme is live for it

classification.quality_note: Royal Caribbean: 'We are the world’s second largest cruise company operating 39 ships in the cruise vacation industry across five brands with an aggregate capacity of approximately 92,650 berths as of December 31, 2011'; 'We compete principally on the basis of exceptional service provided by our crew, innovation and quality of ships, variety of itineraries, choice of destinations and price'; 'We may lose business to competitors throughout the vacation market'; and 'The demand for cruises is affected by international, national and local economic and geopolitical conditions' (its own FY2011 10-K): a cruise-fleet franchise whose demand follows the economies it sells into, by its own account; no disruption theme is live for it. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 7.71x; +92% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -0.60; conservative 2yr -16%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -73.5%/yr (worst year FY02-FY11, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +-1.8%/yr (Q3 cc guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +5.4%/yr (FY02-FY11 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +97.5%/yr (best 2-yr run FY02-FY11); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: RCL (retrospective, 2012-09-28) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 7.71x (96.7% downside to Bear $1 / +12.5% upside to Bull $34) | Adj composite 1.97 vs market 2.57: gap -0.60 [OVERVALUED] | +92% above the EPP floor $16 (9x FY12E $1.75) | Conservative 2-yr case: -16.2% total (-8.1%/yr) | At 17.3x FY12E the 15% hurdle price $40 sits above the BULL case; Net Yields +1.8% in Q2 2012, forward net revenue -1.8% to -0.8% (Q3 2012 net revenue guide at constant currency); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
